correctness.rationale: For every connected graph with root degree n-3, domination of a set containing the root reduces exactly to intersection with the two closed neighborhoods of its nonneighbors. Inclusion-exclusion yields the full polynomial; union-size increments yield a positive binomial polynomial difference and an exact strict stochastic dominance via a mixture/coupling. Exact mean, sharp order endpoints, degree-sum bound, iff equality and minimum-size counts follow by differentiation and monotonicity. Internal edges are irrelevant. The all-parameter mathematical proof covers boundary cases including adjacent exceptional vertices with a zero core-degree. Verification independently examined 33,864 graphs / 2,131,008 root-containing subsets, 360 parameter profiles / 140 adjacent overlaps; finite checks are not infinite certification.

originality.rationale: Originality is claimed only for the two-hole full conditional polynomial together with strict stochastic order, sharp overlap endpoints and the equality classification. Chen–He DOI:10.12677/aam.2026.153090 (March 2026) explicitly leaves the degree n-3 two-nonneighbor case to future study in its conclusion; its theorem treats n-2. The subsequent October 2026 version supplies a general degree-sum bound but still only the n-2 exact case. The current structural stochastic theorem is not implied by either published statement. Full primary texts and relevant published records were examined. Residual risk: unindexed equivalent formulations.
residual_risks: An equivalent theorem may be contained in unindexed or differently named domination-polynomial or stochastic-order literature; semantic and exact searches cannot certify novelty.
The 2021 baseline global-mean full article was not inspected in its entirety, though its stated object is different.
The general degree-sum inequality is already published and is not an originality claim here.

value.rationale: The initiating 2026 paper explicitly singles out the degree n-3 case as future research; here it is solved for all connected graphs, with exact root-conditioned distribution. Strict stochastic order by shared-neighborhood overlap is additional structural information and yields exact extrema and a nontrivial iff equality regime for a general numerical bound. The family includes connected graphs of arbitrary order with free internal edges and all attainable overlap profiles; this is a natural next-degree complete classification rather than an arbitrary finite recomputation.
